record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of analytic multifunctions
record.original_question: Let D be a plane domain, and let K be a polar-valued analytic multifunction on D. Is graph(K) a complete pluripolar set, meaning that there exists a plurisubharmonic function v on D x C such that the set where v = -infinity is exactly graph(K)?

evidence.quote: A natural approach to this problem is to try to show that graph(K1) is a complete pluripolar set, i.e., there exists a plurisubharmonic function v on D x C such that the set where v = -infinity is exactly the graph of K1.
Problem D. Let K be a polar-valued analytic multifunction on D. Is graph(K) a complete pluripolar set?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a domain. A multifunction $K$ on $D$ assigns to each $z \in D$ a nonempty compact subset $K(z) \subset \mathbb{C}$. Such a $K$ is called an analytic multifunction if its graph $\operatorname{graph}(K) = \{(z,w) \in D \times \mathbb{C} : w \in K(z)\}$ is closed in $D \times \mathbb{C}$ and, for every plurisubharmonic function $u$ on $D \times \mathbb{C}$, the function $z \mapsto \sup\{u(z,w) : w \in K(z)\}$ is subharmonic on $D$. The multifunction $K$ is called polar-valued if for each $z \in D$ the fiber $K(z)$ is a polar subset of $\mathbb{C}$ (i.e., there exists a subharmonic function on $\mathbb{C}$, not identically $-\infty$, that equals $-\infty$ on $K(z)$).

A subset $E \subset D \times \mathbb{C}$ is called complete pluripolar if there exists a plurisubharmonic function $v$ on $D \times \mathbb{C}$ such that $E = \{(z,w) \in D \times \mathbb{C} : v(z,w) = -\infty\}$.

Question: Is it true that for every polar-valued analytic multifunction $K$ on $D$, the set $\operatorname{graph}(K)$ is complete pluripolar in $D \times \mathbb{C}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search shows an active body of research on complete pluripolarity of graphs of holomorphic functions and pluripolar hulls (e.g., results that graphs of holomorphic functions with polar singularities are complete pluripolar, and "pluripolar graphs are holomorphic"). However, no source directly resolves the question for general polar-valued analytic multifunctions. The status of this specific question could not be confirmed from the search; it appears to remain an open question in the theory of analytic multifunctions.

status_evidence.title: Pluripolar graphs are holomorphic
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when graphs are pluripolar and shows pluripolar graphs of continuous functions are holomorphic.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist for graphs of single-valued holomorphic functions, but not for general polar-valued analytic multifunctions.

status_evidence.title: The Pluripolar Hull of the Graph of a Holomorphic Function with Polar Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Examines pluripolar hulls of graphs of holomorphic functions with polar singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on complete pluripolarity of graphs are known in the holomorphic case.

status_evidence.title: Complete pluripolar curves and graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs complete pluripolar graphs for certain classes of functions.
status_evidence.claim: Construction techniques exist for special cases but a general answer for polar-valued analytic multifunctions is not provided.
